Assists with development of utilization/care management policies and procedures.

Requires BA/BS in a health related field and minimum of 5 years of clinical experience; or any combination of education and experience, which would provide an equivalent background.
Current, unrestricted RN license in applicable state(s) required.

jobs.title: Senior People Development Program Manager
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

Anduril is building the technology that will transform defense and national security. Our People team is at the center of that mission, ensuring the organization scales as fast as the problems we're solving. Within People, the People & Leadership Development function is moving from early-stage pilots to enterprise-wide programs that reach every manager and leader across a complex, matrixed organization. This role sits at the heart of that transition.

About The Job

We are looking for a Senior People Program Manager to own the scaling of Anduril's leadership development, team coaching, and manager effectiveness programs. Today, we are running a series of successful pilots across the business in coaching, team development, and leadership summits. What we need now is someone who can take what's working, build the roadmap, and operationalize it into a centralized offering that serves the entire company. You will partner directly with People leadership to define the future state, project-plan the path to get there, and execute relentlessly. This person will be equal parts strategist and operator: comfortable presenting program outcomes to senior leadership in a QBR one day and facilitating a team offsite the next.

What You'll Do

Own the transition from pilot to scale for Anduril's leadership and people development programs, including group coaching, manager and high-potential development, team onsites, leadership summits, and team effectiveness offerings.
Build and manage the multi-year program roadmap, defining what a centralized leadership development offering looks like at Anduril by 2027 and the milestones to get there.
Serve as the primary operator and project manager for all people development initiatives, using structured briefs, trackers, and stakeholder communication to keep work on schedule.
Guide team’s evaluation of current pilots with a critical eye: determine what is delivering value and what needs refinement. Use qualitative feedback and quantitative data to inform those calls.
Identify and evaluate technology solutions that can accelerate people development at scale, from coaching platforms to learning management systems.
Help facilitate onsite and offsite experiences, owning the operational end while, when needed, leading facets of team development sessions, leadership workshops, and cross-functional summits.
Present program strategy, progress, and outcomes to senior leadership with clarity and confidence.
Partner across the People org and with business leaders to understand development needs, tailor programming, and build buy-in for new offerings.
Scope the resourcing model: determine when and how to build out a bench of facilitators, coaches, or vendors to support scaled delivery.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in people development, leadership development, organizational development, or program management within a People/HR function.
Demonstrated experience deploying leadership or manager development programs at scale within a large, matrixed organization.
You are motivated by our mission. We are working to solve the biggest problems in defense.
Strong project management instincts: you build structure in ambiguous environments and drive complex, cross-functional work to completion without waiting to be told what to do.
Executive presence and communication skills that allow you to present confidently to senior leaders, facilitate workshops, and craft compelling narratives around program vision and outcomes.
You are both high ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility.
Comfort with data: you can interpret program feedback, build a case for investment, and adjust your approach based on what the numbers say.
You thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and get energy from building something from the ground up rather than maintaining the status quo.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in coaching, executive coaching, or leadership coaching (ICF certification or equivalent is a plus).
Experience designing and facilitating team coaching, offsites, leadership workshops, or similar group development experiences.
Experience at high-growth technology or defense companies that have navigated rapid organizational scaling.
Familiarity with people development technology platforms and their integration into broader HR ecosystems.
Experience building the business case for and standing up a people development function or center of excellence from scratch.

US Salary Range

$146,000—$194,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Rural Resource Navigator

Make a meaningful difference in the lives of veterans, service members and their families while helping strengthen rural Montana communities. Veterans Navigation Network is seeking a compassionate, resourceful and self-motivated Rural Resource Navigator to connect individuals with services that can improve their stability, independence and quality of life.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who understands the unique challenges veterans may face and wants to provide practical, one-on-one support. The successful candidate will build trusted relationships, identify individual needs and help veterans and their families navigate complicated systems and resources.

Location:
Miles City, Montana

Status:
Full-time, in-person

Pay:
$20-$26 per hour

About Veterans Navigation Network

Veterans Navigation Network is a nonprofit organization dedicated to helping service members transition successfully from military service to civilian life. Through resource navigation, intensive case management and advocacy, the organization connects service members, veterans and family members with healthcare, behavioral health, housing, employment, education, legal assistance, suicide prevention, VA benefits and other essential services.

Primary Responsibilities

Conduct outreach to service members, veterans, family members, potential volunteers and community members.
Use motivational interviewing techniques during intake and follow-up conversations.
Help individuals understand available federal and state veterans benefits, services and eligibility requirements.
Assess each individuals needs, abilities, challenges and personal goals.
Create individualized goal, recovery and safety plans.
Connect individuals with healthcare, behavioral health, housing, employment, education, legal and homeless-service resources.
Assist with access to VA disability compensation, survivor benefits, discharge upgrades and other veteran-related programs.
Maintain accurate case notes, records, reports and correspondence using the organizations case management system.
Maintain a current and verified database of community resources.
Follow up regularly with veterans and family members to review progress, paperwork and changing needs.
Coordinate with program leadership to determine when peer mentoring or additional support may be beneficial.
Develop productive relationships with government agencies, veteran service providers, funders, educational institutions and community organizations.
Represent Veterans Navigation Network professionally at meetings, outreach activities and community events.
Protect client privacy and maintain strict confidentiality.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Preferred Education And Experience

An associate degree or higher in business administration, management, social work, social services or a related field is preferred. Relevant substance-use counseling or comparable professional experience may also be considered.

Preferred Experience Includes

Working with veterans, service members or military families.
Suicide prevention and crisis-response practices.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs benefits, programs and services.
Trauma-informed care and interviewing.
Care coordination and case management.
Developing safety, recovery or discharge plans.
Presenting program information, statistics and trends.
Tracking the sustainability of treatment, housing and employment outcomes.
Supporting individuals affected by PTSD, traumatic brain injury, military sexual trauma or substance-use disorders.

Candidates who do not already possess certain preferred training must be able to complete required training within six months of hire.

Skills And Abilities

The ideal candidate will have excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong organizational abilities and a genuine commitment to serving others. This position requires sound judgment, professionalism, empathy and the ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team.

Candidates should be comfortable establishing goals, identifying objectives, managing timelines and following projects through completion. A willingness to learn new programs and take on evolving responsibilities is essential.

Position Requirements

Valid drivers license.
Ability to travel up to 50% for local, statewide and national meetings or events.
Willingness to travel by vehicle or air and complete occasional overnight travel.
Flexibility to work some nights and weekends.
Ability to complete at least six hours of continuing education annually following initial training.

This is a contract-funded position and continued employment is contingent upon the receipt and continued availability of funding. Position sustainability is included in the organizations strategic plan.

Preference will be given to veterans in accordance with the Montana Veteran Hiring Preference Act.

Salary/Compensation: $20.00 - $26.00 per hour

PURPOSE:

The Jewish Board’s Adult Residential Division supports adults with serious and persistent mental illness to live in the community with as much independence as possible. Using a non-judgmental, harm-reduction approach, staff model and guide residents to create and meet personalized recovery goals, develop independent living skills, and live in a healthy and secure manner. Our work is guided by principles that underscore the critical importance of stable housing, use a culturally competent and anti-racist lens, and respect the dignity and legitimacy of each individual’s journey.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Case Manager is the most senior level of direct care staff working within the Jewish Board’s supportive housing programs to help residents live in the community as independently as possible.

KEY ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Resident Support

Carries a caseload and practices person-centered and collaborative service planning with residents.
Is assigned the most complex clients; carries a larger caseload than case associates and case assistants
Ensures service plans are completed and signed by residents according to regulatory guidelines and standards.
Evaluates and assesses independent living skills using a detailed functional assessment tool or supports residents in using tool for self-assessment. Supports residents in meeting individual goals.

Must be able to sit or stand at a desk for prolonged periods while working on a computer
